content:
anya: Heads-up — I found a reproducible correctness drift when activation quantization is enabled (FP8) together with mixed-precision matmul and continuous KV caching. Behaviour shows up only after a few tens of tokens when the cache gets reused across batched requests. :eyes:

anya: Repro command I used:```bash
python perf/repro/act_quant_repro.py \--model redwood/open-6b \--dtype fp8 \--seq 4096 \--batch 4 \--enable-cont-batching
```

anya: Quick summary: outputs diverge from fp16 baseline progressively. Max abs diff (fp8 vs fp16) after 512 tokens: ~2e-4, after 2048 tokens: ~3e-2. Deterministic on our CI GPU (A100).

devon: can you paste the minimal log + profiler slice? curious whether matmul kernel selection flips mid-run or if it's scale-related.

anya: Paste of the key sections:```
[profiler] time_by_op: matmul_fp8_kernel: 42.3%
matmul_fp16_fused: 18.4%
cuda_memcpy_async: 8.7%
kv_cache_copy: 6.1%
activation_quantize: 5.6%
other: 19.0%
```
and a short tensor diff:```py
>>> import numpy as np
>>> np.max(np.abs(out_fp8 - out_fp16))
0.0321
>>> np.mean(np.abs(out_fp8 - out_fp16))
0.0018
```

sam: interesting that matmul_fp8 dominates time_by_op. does kernel selector ever switch to INT8 or fallback? maybe partial casts.

anya: I instrumented kernel selection — it stays on fp8 matmul for the whole sequence. The suspicious bit is the quantization scale update: fp8 activation quant uses a running max/ema per-layer. When the KV cache is reused across batches we never reset the per-sequence acc (we only reset per-request). Combined with continuous batching the acc sees the stale prefix values and then rescales mid-sequence for new tokens. That rescale introduces a non-linear discontinuity which the matmul fp8 kernel doesn't compensate for (it expects a static scale per-kv tile).

tess: so the root cause is mismatch between lifecycle of scale stats and KV cache lifetime? that explains why only long sequences or cont-batching show it.

anya: Exactly. Repro steps to trigger quickly: set seq=4096, small warmup steps so accumulated scale is dominated by earlier prefixes, then send chunked requests that reuse KV.

devon: can you show the code snippet where scale is updated? maybe the calibration had a bug: resetting by token index rather than by cache reset.

anya: Snippet:```py
# activation_quant.py (simplified)
class ActivationQuantizer:
    def update(self, x):
        cur_max = x.abs().max()
        # BAD: global ema not keyed by sequence id or cache version
        self.ema = 0.9 * self.ema + 0.1 * cur_max
        self.scale = compute_scale_from_ema(self.ema)

    def quantize(self, x):
        return quant_fp8(x, self.scale)
```

anya: Proposed fix: tie EMA/scale to the KV cache epoch. When cache is reset (new prefix) stamped with a new version id, clear or re-init per-seq accumulators. Also ensure matmul fp8 kernel receives the live scale metadata per tile, not an earlier cached scale.

sam: we should add a fallback: if scale changes > threshold mid-seq, force recompute with fp16 kernel for safety, then log a regression metric.

tess: small patch idea: on cache reuse add a boolean flag that prevents ema updates until an initial calibration window is seen for the new suffix. That reduces noise.

devon: Any tests? We need a unit/regression test: deterministic seeds + synthetic activations that provoke scale shift.

anya: Added a CI repro test that runs on a small model and asserts L2 difference < 1e-3 after 1024 tokens. Put PR with test here: https://repo.internal/redwood/pull/9876 (WIP).

perf-bot: perf/regression check queued: run on canary infra (A100) — estimated 45m. Report will be posted.

devon: Can you also capture the NVTX traces? want to see if scale-change triggers extra memcpy or kernel relaunch.

anya: NVTX attached in the PR. Observed an extra kernel launch and a memcpy of the scale buffer at the exact token where the EMA jumped > factor 2.

tess: short mitigation we can ship quickly: 1) stop updating EMA across requests by default; 2) opt-in per-model continuous calibration. That gives us safe default.

anya: I'll open two PRs — one for the lifecycle bug and one for the runtime fallback to fp16 when scale-change > X.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued for redd-quant-fix branch to org/dedicated-canary.

devon: nice work. after patch + canary let's run a long-seq stress test (16k tokens, batch 8) and watch metrics: max abs diff and throughput. If fallback hits a lot, we tweak threshold.

anya: Agreed. I'll update the PRs and post results here. If anyone wants to pair on the kernel interface changes ping me.
